transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-08-18 15:00 PDT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Lucas (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Aisha (NovaPay Head Infra), Diego (NovaPay ML Eng), Priya (NovaPay CTO)

Summary: quick sync on throughput optimization, we walked through the 8/16 run numbers, discussed batching and queueing, agreed to new stress test.

00:00 - Maya: hey everybody, thanks for joining, let's kick off, um we're doing the weekly throughput sync, quick status, Lucas over to you for the perf recap
00:28 - Lucas: yeah hi hi, so last run on thursday, um recorded a sustained 140 qps with our current config, that's with concurrency target 12, average batch size ~22, p95 around 410ms, p50 140ms, so still short of the 200 qps goal, we saw some queue buildup at peak
00:54 - Diego: hmm ok when you say queue buildup, that's in the Redwood front-end queue or in our ingress? we saw some spikes in our LB CPU too
01:12 - Lucas: mostly on the inference queue, so requests were waiting to be batched, queue depth hit 600 at one point, which pushed latency up. There was also some backpressure into your LB because of connection saturation
01:38 - Aisha: right, our team saw connection churn, we had to increase worker count, but that increased cost a lot, which we can't sustain for pilot 
01:55 - Maya: yeah cost versus latency tradeoff is classic, want to talk about continuous batching and concurrency tuning, we think increasing concurrency to 16 with a tighter batching window could help, decrease tail latency while preserving throughput
02:15 - Priya: can you clarify, 16 concurrent requests means per GPU instance? how does that map to batch size and to the KV cache hit rate?
02:34 - Lucas: good q, concurrency is per worker process, and the runtime will try to fill batches across concurrency slots, so raising concurrency raises opportunity for larger batches but also more memory pressure on KV cache. We saw KV cache memory climb ~12% during spikes
02:55 - Diego: is that the LRU cache you're referring to? our model has a long context and the KV cache is fairly big, that might explain the memory climbing
03:10 - Lucas: yes LRU-ish, and we have options: either shrink cache TTL for embeddings or pin prefixes for the hottest routes, both help reduce memory but can affect hit rate and increase token compute
03:35 - Maya: quick clarifying note, the config we shared last week had batching window 30ms and max batch 128. In practice we saw average batch ~22 because of request arrival distro
03:52 - Diego: arrival distro is bursty, mostly API traffic from mobile clients, so we get lot of short bursts then quiet periods, not uniform QPS
04:10 - Lucas: that's where queueing strategy matters — we can do adaptive batching: dynamic window that increases up to 80ms when queue depth low to form bigger batches, and closes quickly under backpressure to keep latency stable
04:34 - Aisha: does adaptive batching introduce jitter for tail latency? we can't have p95 > 300ms for the payments flow
04:48 - Lucas: it can, if not tuned. But we can set hard latency SLOs that force the window to close at 80ms or lower for that route. For payments route you'd set a 50ms max batching window and a concurrency floor to keep throughput
05:12 - Priya: what about queue prioritization? can we prioritize payments over analytics? we need to keep payments sub-300ms and analytics can be batchy
05:30 - Ravi: yep we support per-route priority and token-aware routing, you can set a high-priority class that always preempts the queue and triggers smaller batches and higher concurrency for that route
05:47 - Diego: that sounds promising. Any guidance on concurrency numbers? we tried 8 and 12 and saw different behaviour
06:02 - Lucas: rule of thumb: for your model and 1k token average response, concurrency 12-16 tends to hit a good throughput sweet spot; lower concurrency reduces mem overhead but increases chance of small batches; higher concurrency increases batching opportunity but risks memory & context thrash. For NovaPay I recommend testing 16 with window 40ms for payments and 80ms for analytics
06:30 - Maya: also important — autoscale/burst policy, if we set burst capacity you can avoid overprovisioning. For the POC we can configure a burst pool that scales to extra workers for short spikes and then drains
06:50 - Aisha: burst pools sound great but our security team wants to avoid unexpected egress and cost overrun; we need strict caps and alerts
07:05 - Maya: yep we'll set hard caps and alerting thresholds in the console; also add billing guardrails in the account so we don't exceed pilot budget
07:18 - Diego: on the recent run we saw 18% token cost delta compared to baseline due to extra compute from cache misses, curious if quantization changes would lower that
07:34 - Lucas: quantization would reduce memory and per-token compute, but it can impact output quality; for now we recommend tuning batching and cache TTLs before switching quantization for payments-critical flows
07:52 - Priya: any ops guidance on KMS and audit logs? we need to satisfy internal compliance before scaling pilot
08:05 - Maya: yes we'll share the SOC2/ISO doc subset and the audit log export pattern, and we can schedule a compliance walkthrough with our security engineer next week
08:20 - Lucas: returning to throughput, last run metrics: sustained 140 qps, peak 210 qps for 40s, avg batch 22, p95 410ms. We also ran a synthetic run with steady arrivals and that hit 210 qps sustained with 16 concurrency and 60ms window, but real traffic is bursty so results differ
09:01 - Diego: ok that explains the discrepancy; synthetic steady-state is optimistic for us
09:12 - Maya: question for NovaPay — what's the acceptance criteria for the pilot to consider throughput tuned?
09:22 - Priya: primary: payments route p95 < 300ms at target 200 qps sustained for 5 min. Secondary: cost per 1M tokens not exceed baseline by more than 12%. Timeline: want this validated before EOY pilot signoff
09:42 - Maya: good clear criteria. We'll aim the next test at hitting 200 qps sustained for 5 min with p95 < 300ms. Plan: adjust concurrency to 16 for payments route, set batching window 40ms and hard latency cutoff 80ms, enable per-route priority, and tune KV TTLs to reduce cache churn
10:10 - Lucas: I'll prepare a config diff and share it in the sheet. Also propose a stress test plan: 2-hour run with ramp to 250 qps bursts, steady at 200 qps for 30 min blocks, and record per-route metrics and system telemetry
10:34 - Diego: we can run that but need a script that mimics our mobile burst pattern, I'll share the generator we use for mobile traffic so you can mimic bursts
10:45 - Aisha: on infra side, we'll also throttle upstream ingress if we see connection saturation to protect our LB. Might add a small client-side backoff too
10:58 - Maya: ok sounds like we have coordinated plan. A couple of clarifying notes: 1) Redwood will share the spreadsheet with config, logs columns we expect, and the run template; 2) NovaPay to run the 2-hour stress test and upload logs; 3) Redwood SEs to review logs and propose KV tuning changes after the run
11:20 - Ravi: quick note on queueing internals: we have two queue modes, FIFO default and time-compacting mode that will coalesce similar requests into a pseudo-batch even when slots are low. Time-compacting helps with bursty mobile traffic but can increase jitter, so use for analytics not payments
11:45 - Priya: can we get dashboard alerts for queue depth crossing thresholds? we need to be notified at 200, 400, 600 depth
11:59 - Maya: yes, dashboard alerting is supported; we'll set up routes and send to your PagerDuty integration and an email digest for the pilot team
12:18 - Diego: about KV cache pins — you mentioned pinning prefixes earlier, how invasive is that to instrument?
12:31 - Lucas: low invasive, just config map of prefixes per route. We can start with top 20 prefixes from your production logs, pin them with TTL 24h and monitor hit rate delta
12:50 - Aisha: ok we'll extract top prefixes and Diego will provide the list by monday
13:05 - Maya: timeline recap: Lucas will post config diff and the benchmark sheet by fri 8/20; Diego will run stress test and upload logs by 8/25; SEs to review and schedule KV deep-dive wk of 8/23
13:20 - Priya: can you also include cost estimates for the burst pool? we need to present to finance
13:30 - Maya: yes we'll add a cost column to the sheet with estimated delta for different burst sizes
13:40 - Diego: small transcribe note — we saw dropdowns in the run that hinted at GC pauses on the worker, might be another root cause for p95 spikes. We'll include heap profiles in the logs
13:58 - Lucas: good call, include heap and thread dumps where possible. Also include kernel perf counters if you can.
14:12 - Aisha: any blockers from Redwood side for the test?
14:20 - Maya: none. We'll share creds for the pilot console read-only to Diego and Aisha so they can fetch metrics directly. Also we'll provide the pilot config you can paste into your infra for the run
14:36 - Priya: last q, if the run doesn't meet criteria, will Redwood propose quantization options or model variant fallback?
14:44 - Maya: yes fallback plan: we can test a quantized variant in a canary pool or fallback to a smaller context model for payments route; we'll only do that post-analysis since quality is critical
14:58 - Diego: cool. That's it from me
15:05 - Maya: thanks everyone; we'll follow up with sheet and schedule.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-attributions and some imperfect punctuation from auto-transcribe. References: benchmark sheet link (shared in chat): https://redwood-internal.sheets/novapay-poc-benchmarks (placeholder), run template: /docs/poc/stress-run-template
notes: Shared artifacts: benchmark spreadsheet, run template, SOC2/ISO summary (to be shared).
